flakes.test: src/specs/companions.spec.tsx > Switching views > opens a plan's editor as it was left
flakes.cause: Two causes, both fixed. First (#232), the spec: it scrolled the pane to line 200 right after typing at the top of a restored one, and typing scrolls the caret into view in the editor's next measure, which on a slow frame came after the spec's scroll and put the pane back at the top, so its saved place was the first line; the spec now waits two frames after typing. Second, the app: a plan restored in Canvas, which scales the pane in, aimed at its saved line from the live zoom while CodeMirror's line heights were still at its last measured scale, as a transform alone doesn't make it measure; on a busy page the restore settled on a wrong line (the Steps heading) before the editor measured again. The restore now asks for a measure and waits while the editor's scale lags the pane's (libraries/viewers markdown/scroll.ts).

flakes.test: src/specs/preferences.spec.tsx > Preferences Addons > when murmur is not installed > stops an install on Cancel
flakes.signature: Cannot find element with locator: getByRole\('dialog', \{ name: 'Preferences' \}\).*getByRole\('button', \{ name: 'Install' \}\)|locator\.click: Timeout \d+ms exceeded[\s\S]*name: 'Cancel'
flakes.cause: The demo's install ran on its wall clock (1.2 s a step) while the test clicked Install, then Cancel: on a loaded runner Cancel came during the install's check, which keeps what it installed, so Install never came back (Linux), or after the install had finished, so there was no Cancel to click (macOS). Reproduced with a pause before Cancel. The specs now open the install held at its first step (`&install=held`), so Cancel lands mid-download however slow the machine.

flakes.signature: TypeError: expect\.element is not a function
flakes.cause: Unknown, not reproduced: every test of the file failed at its first expect.element (openWorkspace's), and its rerun passed. Browser mode adds expect.element through a module script of its own (@vitest/browser's expect-element.js) in each file's page, before the tester; a page where that script didn't load or ran against another copy of vitest runs without it. Vite optimizing a dependency mid-run would do it, but a cold-cache run of the behaviour project optimized everything up front. Its test is the whole file, as the whole file fails.
